terms.gloss: turn out, fall out (well, as one wished)
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, intransitive, with an adverb or ut
evidence: Cic. Att. 3.7.1: sānē ita cadēbat ut vellem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 5.19.1: cum aliter rēs cecidisset ac putāssēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says things “fall” well or badly, as dice fall: bene cecidit, it turned out well.
Not found in Lewis & Short or the loci collections in this form; Traupman is the only evidence. Cicero uses the verb with ita … ut and aliter.

sources: Lewis & Short: cado
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 110.
